title: Captured German SS documents at the National Archives
summary: Peter Levenda tells of Captured German SS documents at the National Archives, about 1930s-1940s documents; research in 2000s at Washington, D.C., and says they saw it or took part. As told, not a fact.
place_text: National Archives / Library of Congress, Washington DC

tellings.quote: archives, but I wanted to see the captured German documents from the war. They had this a bunch of microfilm.

plain: Peter Levenda, an author described as a historian, says that in the 2000s he went to the US National Archives in Washington to read German documents captured at the end of the Second World War. He says they were kept on microfilm and included records of the SS, the Nazi elite force run by Heinrich Himmler, from the 1930s and 40s.
